stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many birdwatchers assume that the brilliant red of a male northern cardinal comes from pigments the bird produces within its own body. ______ the color comes from carotenoids, compounds the bird takes in from the seeds and berries it eats. Researchers have found that a cardinal kept on a diet poor in carotenoids molts into plumage that is noticeably duller, closer to brown than to scarlet.
explanation: The first sentence gives a common belief: that cardinals make their own red pigment. The next sentence replaces that belief with the true fact: the color comes from food. When a mistaken assumption is followed by a correction, 'Actually' is the word that marks the correction.

A.why: You read the second sentence as a sample of what birdwatchers assume. It doesn't illustrate that belief. It overturns it, so 'For instance' gets the relationship wrong.

C.why: This is the trap. Both sentences are about where the cardinal's color comes from, so you picked a same-direction word without checking the logic. The second sentence contradicts the first rather than matching it.

D.why: The belief doesn't cause the carotenoid fact. 'As a result' claims a cause-and-effect link, but the real relationship is a correction.

subtype_name: Expectation, then surprise (However / Nonetheless / That said / Actually)

rated_why: Assumption contradicted by evidence in straightforward fashion

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Linguist Rosa Albani has catalogued several features that the Creole languages of the Caribbean share with the European languages from which they partly descend: much of their vocabulary, many of their sound patterns, and some of their basic word order. ______ their verb systems, which mark tense and aspect with separate particles placed before the verb, bear little resemblance to any European model.
explanation: The first sentence lists ways the Creoles resemble European languages, which leads you to expect more resemblance. The second sentence gives an exception: the verb systems don't resemble European ones. An exception that goes against the expectation calls for 'However.'

B.why: This is the trap. Both sentences compare Creoles with European languages, so 'Likewise' feels natural. But the first sentence is about similarity and the second is about difference, so they point in opposite directions.

C.why: The first sentence names a category ('several features'), and you took the verb systems to be one member of it. But the features in that category are shared, and the verb systems are not shared. They are an exception, not an example.

D.why: Nothing in the list of shared features leads to the verb systems being different. 'Therefore' claims a conclusion the passage never draws.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Ottilie Brandt's career as a composer was crowded with public triumphs: three operas staged in Vienna, a symphony premiered to acclaim in Leipzig, and a coronation mass commissioned by the Saxon court. ______ Brandt herself regarded a set of unpublished songs for voice and piano, written for her sister and performed only in the family parlor, as the finest work she ever produced.
explanation: The first sentence lists grand public successes, which leads you to expect Brandt valued those works most. The second sentence reveals that she ranked a small private work above all of them. That pivot against the list calls for 'Still.'

A.why: This is the trap. You saw a list of achievements and treated the songs as one more item on it. But the second sentence ranks the songs above the whole list, which works against it rather than adding to it.

B.why: The public triumphs don't explain why Brandt preferred private songs. 'Consequently' claims a cause that isn't there.

D.why: The second sentence doesn't restate the first. It introduces a new judgment that cuts against it, so a restatement word doesn't fit.

rated_why: Personal preference contradicts public success; still bridges internal and external values

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The designers of the Carrow Footbridge were confident that its stiff steel deck, anchored by twelve tensioned cables, would barely move under even the heaviest pedestrian traffic. ______ within an hour of the bridge's opening, crowds unconsciously falling into step with the deck's slight sideways sway had set it swinging so noticeably that officials closed it to the public.
explanation: The first sentence describes what the designers expected: a deck that would barely move. The second sentence reports the opposite: the deck swung so much that the bridge had to close. An outcome that defeats the expectation calls for 'However.'

A.why: You linked the stiff design to the outcome as if the design produced it as planned. 'Accordingly' signals a consequence that fits the setup, but this outcome contradicts it.

C.why: The second sentence doesn't describe the designers' confidence in more precise terms. It reports a result that disproves that confidence, so 'Specifically' is the wrong relationship.

D.why: This is the trap. Both sentences are about how the deck moves, so an addition word seems fine. But 'the deck barely moves' and 'the deck swung until the bridge closed' contradict each other.

subtype_name: Expectation, then surprise (However / Nonetheless / That said / Actually)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Producing a color woodcut in the traditional Japanese manner starts with carving a separate block for each color, a task that newcomers to printmaking often assume is the most demanding stage of the process. ______ many practitioners, including printmaker Keiko Hale, report that the final stage, aligning each block on the paper so that the colors meet without gaps or overlaps, takes far longer to master.
explanation: The first sentence gives an assumption: carving is the hardest stage. The second sentence reports that experienced printmakers find a different stage harder. A correction of that assumption calls for 'That said.'

B.why: The newcomers' assumption isn't the reason practitioners find alignment harder. 'For this reason' claims a cause, but the real relationship is contrast.

C.why: This is the trap. Both sentences talk about which stage is demanding, so they seem parallel. But they name different stages and disagree about which one is hardest.

D.why: The passage mentions stages, so a step word is tempting. But the sentence after the blank describes the final stage, not the first, and its job is to push back on the assumption, not to put steps in order.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When cholera cases rose in the city's port district in 1866, the sanitary board recommended that residents burn sulfur in their homes to purify the air, which board members believed carried the disease. ______ physician Clara Denholm, convinced that the illness spread through contaminated water, persuaded district officials to seal three public wells. New cases fell sharply within weeks.
explanation: The board recommends one approach based on its belief that the air carries the disease. Denholm rejects that belief and takes a different course. Replacing the recommended approach with a rival one is a contrast, so the answer is 'However.'

A.why: This is the trap. Both sentences are about responses to the outbreak, so 'Likewise' sounds natural. But Denholm's theory and action oppose the board's rather than matching them.

B.why: The board's advice didn't lead Denholm to seal the wells. She acted against its reasoning, so 'Hence' invents a cause.

D.why: Sealing wells isn't an example of the board's air-purifying advice. It's a different option that replaces that advice.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Because spinach is famously rich in iron, it may seem an ideal food for people trying to raise their iron levels. ______ much of that iron is bound to oxalic acid, a compound that sharply limits how much of the mineral the body can absorb. Some studies suggest that only a few percent of the iron in spinach ever reaches the bloodstream.
explanation: The phrase 'may seem' sets up an appearance: spinach looks like an ideal source of iron. The next sentence undercuts it: most of that iron can't be absorbed. When reality contradicts an appearance, the answer is 'However.'

A.why: This is the trap. Both sentences are about the iron in spinach, so an addition word seems fine. But the second sentence argues against the first rather than adding to it.

B.why: Spinach's reputation doesn't cause its iron to be bound to oxalic acid. 'Thus' claims a conclusion that doesn't follow.

C.why: 'Namely' would mean the second sentence restates, more precisely, why spinach is ideal. Instead it explains why spinach falls short, so it isn't a restatement.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Planners in the city of Merrow had long believed that widening its main commuter road from four lanes to six would ease rush-hour congestion. ______ within three years of the expansion, average commute times on the road had returned to their earlier levels, because the added capacity attracted drivers who had previously taken other routes or traveled at other hours.
explanation: 'Had long believed' sets up an expectation: wider roads mean less congestion. The second sentence gives the actual result, which is that congestion returned. When a belief is followed by the facts that correct it, 'In reality' fits.

A.why: 'To that end' would introduce a step taken to achieve the planners' goal. The second sentence reports that the goal wasn't reached, not a way of pursuing it.

C.why: This is the trap. Both sentences are about the road and its traffic, so an addition word seems fine. But the result contradicts the planners' belief instead of building on it.

D.why: Returning commute times aren't an illustration of the planners' belief. They are evidence against it, so 'For example' gets the relationship wrong.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: For decades, highway engineers assumed that packing more steel reinforcing bar into a concrete bridge deck would lengthen its service life, since steel resists the pulling forces that concrete handles poorly. When inspectors in one state surveyed four hundred decks built in the 1980s, they expected the most heavily reinforced ones to be in the best condition. ______ those decks showed the widest surface cracking, because closely spaced bars kept the concrete above them from settling evenly as it cured.
explanation: The sentences before the blank set up an expectation: more steel should mean a longer-lasting deck, so the most heavily reinforced decks should look best. The sentence after the blank gives the opposite result, with those decks cracking worst. A finding that undercuts an expectation calls for a contrast word, so 'However' is correct.

A.why: 'Accordingly' says the cracking follows from the inspectors' expectation. It doesn't. The cracking goes against what they expected. You probably saw that both sentences are about heavily reinforced decks and never checked which way the logic runs.

B.why: 'Furthermore' adds a point that supports the one before it. The cracking doesn't support the engineers' assumption. It contradicts it. Try putting 'and also' between the sentences: 'they expected the best condition, and also those decks cracked worst' doesn't make sense.

D.why: 'For example' introduces one case drawn from a larger group. The cracked decks aren't an example of the inspectors' expectation. They are the evidence that the expectation was wrong.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over a forty-year career, the cartographer Ilse Varga produced nautical charts, railway atlases, and city plans that earned her several international awards and were reprinted in a dozen languages. ______ Varga herself regarded a far more modest project as her finest achievement: a hand-inked map of the footpaths around her childhood village, drawn as a gift for her neighbors and never published.
explanation: The first sentence lists Varga's celebrated, prize-winning work, which leads you to expect that she would value it most. The second sentence ranks something else above all of it: a small map that was never published and won nothing. That turns against the list of successes, so you need a concession word like 'Still'.

A.why: 'Specifically' would mean the village map is one of the awarded works, described more precisely. It isn't. It was never published and won no prizes. The first sentence names a group of works and the second names a single map, and that pattern may have suggested a group-then-member relationship that isn't really there.

B.why: This is the trap for a string of successes. Both sentences praise Varga's work, so 'Moreover' can sound like it piles on one more accomplishment. But the second sentence places a modest project above the whole celebrated list, and that is a turn against the list, not an addition to it.

C.why: 'As a result' claims that Varga's awards and reprints caused her to prize the village map. Nothing in the text connects the two. The map matters to her in spite of the fame, not because of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Silica aerogel may seem too delicate for demanding jobs. A block of the material is more than 95 percent air by volume, and a thin slab can crumble if pinched between two fingers. ______ engineers have relied on it to insulate subsea oil pipelines and electronics aboard Mars rovers, settings in which its exceptional ability to block heat matters more than its brittleness.
explanation: The first two sentences build an impression: aerogel 'may seem' too fragile to be useful, and they give evidence of how easily it breaks. The last sentence reports that engineers use it anyway in very demanding settings. That goes against the impression the passage set up, so you need 'Nonetheless', a word that concedes the fragility and then moves past it.

A.why: 'Therefore' would mean engineers chose aerogel because it crumbles easily. Its fragility is a drawback they work around, not the reason they use it. Before you pick a cause word, check whether the first fact actually leads to the second.

C.why: 'For instance' would make pipelines and rovers examples of aerogel's delicacy. They show the reverse: tough jobs where aerogel succeeds even though it is fragile.

D.why: 'Likewise' signals a similar point heading the same direction. The text sets up fragility and then reports demanding uses, which point in opposite directions. Both sentences are about aerogel, but sharing a topic doesn't mean they share a direction.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: For decades, ornithologists assumed that Kessler's warbler, a songbird weighing barely ten grams, could not cross the Gulf of Mexico in a single flight. A bird so small, they reasoned, would have to break the journey into short hops, stopping on oil platforms and barrier islands to refuel. ______ when researchers fitted a dozen warblers with featherweight tracking tags last spring, every bird flew the entire 900-kilometer route without landing.
explanation: The first two sentences state a belief: the warbler must stop to refuel on the way across. The last sentence reports what the tags showed, which is that every bird flew the whole route without stopping. That result goes against the belief, so you need a word that signals a reversal. "However" does that.

A.why: You saw that both sentences are about the warbler's crossing and picked a cause word without checking which way the logic runs. The ornithologists' reasoning didn't cause the birds to fly nonstop. The tracking data proved that reasoning wrong.

B.why: You treated the tracking result as one more point in support of what came before. Try putting "and also" between the sentences: "they must stop to refuel, and also every bird flew without landing" contradicts itself. The new fact undercuts the belief, so an addition word can't work.

D.why: "Similarly" says the second idea is like the first. A nonstop flight is the opposite of a journey broken into short hops, so the two sentences aren't alike at all.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over a forty-year career, folklorist Ilona Varga recorded more than two thousand oral tales in Hungarian farming villages, published a seven-volume catalog of their recurring plots, and founded the archive in Szeged that still houses her tapes. ______ Varga counted none of these as her chief accomplishment. What mattered most, she wrote late in life, was a single afternoon's recording of her grandmother singing a ballad no one else remembered.
explanation: The first sentence lists major achievements, so you'd expect Varga to be proudest of one of them. The next sentence says she wasn't. She ranked one small recording above everything on the list. That's a turn against what the list leads you to expect, so you need a concession word. "Still" fits.

A.why: You picked a cause word because both sentences are about Varga's work. Her catalog and archive didn't cause her to value them less. The second sentence pushes against the list rather than following from it.

B.why: This is the list-of-successes trap. You read the opening as a run of achievements and expected another one to be added. But the next sentence sets every item on that list below something else, which is a pivot, not an addition.

D.why: "Specifically" would mean the next sentence restates the list more precisely, for example by naming which achievement she meant. Instead it rejects all of them as her chief accomplishment. Nothing is being zoomed in on.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When a measles outbreak reached Harlan County in 2023, epidemiologist Rahul Mehta urged officials to open one large vaccination site at the county convention center. A single well-staffed location, he argued, would reach the most residents in the least time. ______ the county health board, noting that many families lacked cars and that bus service was sparse, sent small mobile clinics to church lots and grocery stores instead.
explanation: The first two sentences give Mehta's advice: open one central site. The last sentence says the board did something different and sent mobile clinics "instead." Advice that was turned down calls for a contrast word, and "However" signals that the board went the other way.

A.why: You assumed the board's decision followed from Mehta's advice because both sentences are about the vaccination plan. "Accordingly" means the board acted on his recommendation, but the word "instead" tells you it chose the opposite.

B.why: "Likewise" says the board did something similar to what Mehta proposed. Many small mobile clinics are the opposite of one central site, so the two plans aren't alike.

C.why: "For instance" would make the mobile clinics an example of Mehta's single-site plan. They don't illustrate his plan. They replace it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Archaeologists working at Kellanmor, an Iron Age settlement on a windswept northern coast, long assumed that its eleven stone towers were grain stores. Large clay jars of the kind used for keeping barley had turned up beside nine of the eleven structures, and the towers' thick walls seemed built to keep stored food dry. ______ a 2021 analysis of residue inside the jars detected barley in only two of them; most had held fish oil, which suggests the towers were places for processing fish rather than for storing grain.
explanation: The first sentences set up a long-held assumption: the towers were grain stores, and the jars seemed to prove it. The sentence after the blank reports a result that undercuts that belief, since barley turned up in only two jars and fish oil in most of them. That is the opposite direction from what the setup leads you to expect, so you need a concession or contrast word. "However" signals that the new evidence goes against the assumption.

A.why: You saw that both sentences are about the jars and assumed the second follows from the first. "Consequently" says the residue findings were caused by the grain-store assumption. In fact they contradict it, and nothing in the first sentences produces them.

C.why: You treated the residue analysis as one more piece of evidence on the same side. "Furthermore" adds support to the grain-store idea, but the fish-oil finding argues against it. Try saying "and also" between the sentences and it sounds wrong, so an addition word can't be right.

D.why: You read the residue analysis as an instance of something the first sentences describe. "For example" would need it to be one case of the grain-store claim. It's evidence that overturns the claim, not a sample of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over two decades, a community program to revive the Teshwa language has produced a 30,000-word dictionary, a weekly radio broadcast, and a reading curriculum now taught in eleven schools. Linguists studying endangered languages often cite it as a model for other revival efforts. ______ when researchers surveyed Teshwa families in 2022, they found that the share of children speaking the language at home had barely moved, rising from 4 percent to just 5 percent in twenty years.
explanation: The first two sentences list the program's achievements and its reputation as a model. From that, you would expect children's use of the language at home to have grown a lot. The sentence after the blank says it grew only from 4 percent to 5 percent, so it undercuts the impression of success. "Even so" concedes the achievements and then turns against them, which is exactly that relationship.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. Both sentences are about the program, so you assumed the survey result follows from the achievements. "As a result" claims the dictionary, broadcast and curriculum caused the tiny one-point gain. The text presents that gain as disappointing despite all the work.

B.why: You read the survey as one more item on the list of accomplishments. A one-point rise over twenty years isn't presented as a success. It works against the list, so an addition word points the wrong way.

D.why: You took the survey as an illustration of the program's success. "For instance" needs the next sentence to show one case of what came before. This sentence shows the program falling short, not an example of it working.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Traffic consultants hired by the city of Marlow recommended widening Harbor Avenue from four lanes to six, predicting that the extra space would cut rush-hour travel times along the route by roughly a third. The city council heard the proposal in 2019. ______ the council voted to narrow the avenue to two car lanes and give the reclaimed space to a protected bus corridor; three years later, average commutes on the route were eight minutes shorter than before.
explanation: The first sentences set up an expectation: experts recommended widening the road, and the council heard the plan. The sentence after the blank shows the council doing the reverse, narrowing the avenue instead. Because the second sentence goes against the advice in the first, you need a contrast word, and "However" marks that turn.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You assumed the council followed the consultants because the sentences are about the same road. "Accordingly" means the council acted in line with the advice, but it rejected the advice and did the opposite.

B.why: You treated the council's decision as a parallel to the consultants' plan. "Likewise" says the second action resembles the first. Narrowing a road isn't like widening it. It's the reverse.

C.why: You read the second sentence as a more precise restatement of the proposal. "Namely" zooms in on what was just said, but the bus-corridor plan isn't a detail of the widening proposal. It replaces that proposal.
